sections.sectionSummaryBrief: This section introduces the verse about dwelling in sukkos and discusses the necessity of knowledge as part of the mitzvah, the paradox of settlement within a surrounding light, and the unique unity of all Israel in the sukkah.

translations.translation: "You shall dwell in sukkos for seven days; every native-born Jew shall dwell in sukkos."
(And the reason for this is)
"So that your generations may know that I caused the children of Israel to dwell in sukkos when I brought them out of the land of Egypt, etc."
And from the language of the verse
("so that your generations may know, etc.")
we learn
that this knowledge is
(not only a matter of the intention of the mitzvah,
but rather)
a part of the fulfillment of the mitzvah
(as is also evident from the language of the Alter Rebbe in his Shulchan Aruch).
And the precise points of our Nesi'im regarding this are known:
Why is this knowledge so crucial
that it is a part of the mitzvah?
And also, what is the meaning of "You shall dwell in sukkos"?
For a sukkah is a level of encompassing light (makif), and the matter of settlement
(for "teishvu" also includes the interpretation of settlement)
specifically relates to a level of internal light (pnimi),
and from the fact that it says "You shall dwell in sukkos," it proves that even after the dwelling, it remains a level of encompassing light,
and the matter of settlement must be within the encompassing light.
Also, one must understand what is written: "Every native-born Jew shall dwell in sukkos,"
for the command "You shall dwell in sukkos" is for all of Israel; what does "every native-born Jew shall dwell in sukkos" add?
And in the command "You shall dwell in sukkos," it says "seven days," whereas in the command "every native-born, etc.," it says "shall dwell in sukkos" without specification.
And behold, from this verse
("every native-born Jew shall dwell in sukkos")
we learn
that all of Israel are fit to dwell in one sukkah.
And it must be said:
Behold, the matter of the unity of all of Israel
(the matter of "You are standing today, all of you")
exists also throughout the entire year,
to the extent that the mitzvah of loving a fellow Jew
[the reason for which is that they are all compatible and have one Father for all of them
(the matter of unity)
as explained in Tanya]
is the entire Torah, and the rest is its explanation,
meaning that every mitzvah is like an explanation and detail of the matter of the unity of all of Israel,
so why is this specifically emphasized in the mitzvah of sukkah?
And also, one must understand what is written
(before this)
"And you shall take for yourselves on the first day the fruit of a beautiful tree, branches of date palms, a branch of a thick-leaved tree, and willows of the brook,"
and it is known
that this mitzvah has a connection to the matter of the sukkah,
which is why the preferred mitzvah is that the taking of the Four Species should be in the sukkah.
For this is also the connection of the taking of the Four Species to the level of Daas (knowledge),
(similar to "so that they may know" regarding the sukkah),
as it is stated in the writings of the Arizal
that the intent of the waving of the lulav is to draw down Daas to the Nukva of Zeir Anpin, which stands at the chest of Zeir Anpin
(which is why the lulav and its species must touch the chest).

sections.sectionSummaryBrief: This section explains the general service of drawing down the encompassing light into settlement, paralleling the progression from faith to comprehension throughout one's life and even in Moshe Rabbeinu's level.

translations.translation: B)
And this will be understood by prefacing the matter of drawing down the encompassing light with settlement
("You shall dwell in sukkos")
in the service of G-d as it is throughout the life of a person in general,
and likewise in every single day.
For although this matter in its essence is during the festival of Sukkos,
"You shall dwell in sukkos,"
nevertheless, the Torah was stated in generalities and specifics,
and there is a semblance of this matter also throughout the entire year.
And the explanation is:
Behold, the two matters of encompassing light (makif) and internal light (pnimi) in the service of G-d in general are faith and comprehension.
And first, the matter of the encompassing light of the sukkah must be explained,
and afterwards, "You shall dwell in sukkos" must be explained,
for the beginning of service is in the level of faith.
For every single Jew,
as soon as he comes into the world,
has within him a level of faith,
as our Sages said,
"Israel are believers, children of believers."
For this is a true description, according to the Torah of truth, of every single Jew.
And after he reaches the age of education, etc., and comes to possess Daas (intellect),
behold, what was initially for him in the level of faith and encompassing light
is drawn into a level of internalization and settlement,
to the extent that this becomes his entire existence.
Nevertheless, even then he has a level of faith,
for after and through the drawing down of the encompassing light
(what was previously in the level of encompassing light)
into internalization,
a higher level of encompassing light is drawn down,
and this encompassing light is in the level of faith.
And likewise, throughout all the days of his life,
the more he elevates himself in his service and in his comprehension,
what was initially for him in the level of faith
is drawn into understanding and comprehension,
and his faith is in a more elevated level
[and similar to the general collective of the children of Israel,
that initially they were included among the nations of the world,
whose faith is only in the level of the power of the actor within the acted-upon,
and afterwards they were elevated, etc., so that their faith was in the level of the One who transcends the world,
as explained in the Siddur, Shaar HaChag HaMatzos, at its beginning].
To the extent that our Sages said,
"Believe in every matter of Moshe Rabbeinu,"
even though Moshe was the ultimate perfection of wisdom,
behold, even after the perfection of comprehension, there are matters that are in the level of faith, beyond comprehension.
And on the contrary,
the more one comprehends, the comprehension itself necessitates that there are matters that are beyond intellect,
to the extent of the statement,
"The ultimate knowledge is that we do not know You."
